about: Allowlists for the VIB-65 guardrail rules in tools/eslint/rules/guardrails.mjs. Each rule runs on its scope; a file is exempt only if an allow entry names it, and every entry needs a reason. Inline eslint-disable of vibtra/* rules is refused, so this file is the only way out.

allow.reason: LocalSigner is the one place that opens a sealed private key and signs with it.
The ES256 signing primitive and the GuardSigner port that LocalSigner implements.
The vault sealer seals and opens private keys at rest; it never signs.
The signing-key store row mappers must name the sealed_private_key column; they hand out sealed bytes, never an opened key.
Tests mint throwaway keys and sign fixtures to drive the real verifiers.
The engine grader signs throwaway fixture policies with a key it generates and discards in the same run.
The rule itself must name the identifiers it bans.
loadRegistryConfig is where the registry reads and checks its environment.
The CLI entry hands process.env to loadRegistryConfig and reads HOST and PORT for listen().

Baseline at VIB-65: createRegistryServer reads VIBTRA_TEST_CLOCK, VIBTRA_LANDING_DIST, VIBTRA_GUARD_CONSOLE_DIST, VIBTRA_GUARD_SERVER_URL and REGISTRY_FREE_BUDGET_HOURS. Every one is in the config's known-variable list, so boot still refuses typos; moving them into RegistryConfig changes createRegistryServer's options, which many tests build directly.
Baseline at VIB-65: registryLogLevel reads LOG_LEVEL from process.env because bootLog and the Fastify logger need a level before the config is parsed, so a config error can still be logged.
Baseline at VIB-65: createRegistryAuth re-checks that test auth is never on with NODE_ENV=production, a second guard after loadRegistryConfig.
Baseline at VIB-65: the request desk reads VIBTRA_TEST_GRANT_TTL_S (listed in the config's known variables) when its options pass no env; tests pass their own env.
The local VaultSealer owns the vault.v1. prefix and publishes it as envelopePrefix.
The gate-key sealer owns the vgk.v1. prefix for the jwks table; no VaultSealer seals those rows.
Tests build fake sealers with their own prefixes (kms.v1. and others) to prove the tripwire reads envelopePrefixes.
